name: Smith JM press
cue: Elbows forward; lower the bar toward your chin, then press up.
research: JM press on a Smith machine (science audit table B: the Smith JM press as the overhead extension and pushdown alternative, a triceps press between a close-grip bench press and a skull crusher). Lying flat on a bench (the Smith flat press body: back pad 0.186 H above the floor, trunk -90, hips 15, knees 100, shins vertical, feet flat), narrow grip: hands 0.085 H each side of the midline (about the width of the shoulder joints, 0.09 H, so the forearms stay near vertical in the frontal plane), pronated. The bar rides on vertical rails 0.36 H out, 0.3 H toward the head from the hips, over the base of the neck: 0.033 H toward the head from the shoulder joints, so the arms lean 4 deg toward the head at the lockout. Bottom: the bar 0.078 H (about 14 cm) above the base of the neck and upper chest, elbow flexion 135 (the forearms fold toward the upper arms, the elbows have travelled forward of the bar to 0.15 H ahead of the shoulder joints and 0.03 H above them: upper arm about 80 deg from vertical toward the feet); top: a soft lockout (elbow 20) with the bar 0.36 H above the shoulders. The elbow angles at both ends set the bar heights (bisection on the IK solution), the bar and the elbows run evenly between; the pole of the arm IK points the elbows forward and up (0.25, 0.55, 1). Scapulae retracted and depressed. Muscles: the three triceps heads primary, the chest amber (the chest helps in a press).

targets.note: Design values for a JM press on the flat-bench body: the bar over the base of the neck at the bottom (elbows 135, forward of the bar) and a soft lockout (elbow 20) at the top; shoulder angles are the IK solution for a 0.085 H grip.

camera.note: Research view az 90 / el 10 (profile: the bar path and the elbows travelling forward). Turned 50 deg toward the foot end and raised 20 deg (az 40 / el 30, 53 deg off the research view): in a JM press the forearms fold toward the head, so the back of the upper arm faces the feet and the triceps read as a belly on each upper arm while the elbows swing from forward to overhead; from the head end (az 150) the arms show their biceps side and the triceps glow all but disappears. The near plate and rail stand beside the head, behind the shoulder from this side. The bench stands on two feet and a centre rail with a foot plate under the feet only, so the floor under the name stays clear.
